instruction: Halt all progress. Make a list of tasks I need to complete, and stop me if I try to move forward before finishing everything - whether it's learning the things I said I would, adding necessary items, and so on.
how_to_lift: Set halted=false, or clear it item by item: an item with status 'done' stops counting. The loop refuses to start new product work while halted=true and any BLOCKER is open.
what_is_still_allowed_while_halted: Recording his answers into this file / the decision stores.
what_is_forbidden_while_halted: The PR #70 self check-in acting on the branch (merging main in, pushing). It may REPORT only.
note_on_the_pr_checkin: A send_later Routine (trig_012ir9As53TTiGMFBw9Pmvps) fires ~15:17Z. The delete_trigger tool was not available in this session, so it could not be cancelled. When it fires it must read this file, do nothing, and say so.

owner_confirmed.what: Eitan verified the blocker was really set and asked that it STAY in place. He will return with answers and timelines for every item.
owner_confirmed.he_asked_for: Help defining the PARAMETERS for each item - what a good answer to each one actually has to contain - explicitly NOT necessarily in the session that created this file.
owner_confirmed.TO_ANY_FUTURE_SESSION: Do not treat this as permission to resume. Eitan tested the halt on purpose and asked for it to hold. When he returns, the useful move is to help him SHAPE each answer (see answer_parameters below), not to lift the halt and build. Only Eitan lifts it, in plain words.

answer_parameters.why: Eitan asked for help with the parameters of each item. These are what a COMPLETE answer to each one has to contain, so he is never guessing what 'done' means for his own homework.
B1: One section per element type: skill, tool, prompt, command, connector, design, format, model, creation, plus package.
Each section needs four things: what GOOD looks like, what MEDIOCRE looks like, what DISQUALIFIES outright, and the OBSERVABLE SIGNAL that decides which bucket a given element falls in.
The observable signal is the part that makes it machine-checkable - 'is useful' cannot be measured, 'has a runnable command and a named target version' can.
Rule of thumb for whether a criterion is finished: could a script sort 100 elements into good/mediocre/disqualified using only what is written down?
Claude can run this as an interview using real good and bad examples from the live hub, and write the answers in Eitan's own words.
B2: B2a/B2b are done when the key exists AND Eitan tells Claude the SECRET NAME to wire it under - a key nobody names is not wired.
B2b specifically must be a SEPARATE key from the analysis pipeline's, or the video lane will drain it again within a day and 153 tasks re-block.
B2d is done when Eitan says a monthly ceiling in dollars, not just yes/no - an uncapped 'yes' cannot be enforced by any guardrail.
D1: Name the host AND who administers it. 'Oracle' is not an answer until the account exists.
D2: A number per metric and a date. Confidence / Completeness / Sales, each 0-100, each with the date it should be true by.
S1: A date and a block of time. The session is ~300 decisions; it does not fit in fifteen minutes.
S2_S3_S4_L1: These are done when the information reaches Claude in writing - a link, a paste, or a spoken walk-through captured in the repo. Nothing here is done by being decided privately.
